expectation: Nuclear stain in naive and stem-like memory T cells (plus some NK and innate lymphoid cells). In this gut mucosa it should be dense in lymphoid aggregates and follicle T zones, with scattered single nuclei in the lamina propria. It should be absent from the epithelium.
observed: A: yellow haze outside the tissue and bright lit spots at lymphoid aggregates. B/C: crypt epithelium is dim, with scattered small dots in the stroma and one debris streak and blob. D: round nuclear-sized cells, many bright, beside negative blue nuclei. E: in a CD3-dense aggregate, most CD3 cells are TCF1+ (white).
why: Bright nuclear TCF1 cells sit in lymphoid aggregates and largely on CD3+ cells, which is the expected T-cell pattern; background haze and debris do not account for it.
notes: TCF1 lights nuclei in lymphoid aggregates, overlapping much of the CD3 signal, while the epithelium stays dim. There is glow outside the tissue and some bright debris in B, but the cellular pattern in the aggregates is convincing.
